newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks buoyant in handover run-up.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks buoyant in handover run-up.

text.p: Hong Kong's stock market enters the final month of colonial rule at all-time highs and should continue to ride a wave of handover optimism ahead of the territory's change in sovereignty, analysts said.

Share prices drove deep into record ground last week and could continue moving higher in the coming week, although some consolidation may lie ahead before the blue chip Hang Seng Index hits its next target of 15,000 points.
"It would not be surprising to see it pushing higher next week," said South China Holdings vice chairman Howard Gorges.

"Of course, if it does get somewhere near 15,000 then some consolidation could start, but it has got considerable strength and there is plenty of liquidity around so I would not want to be short on it," he added.
The Hang Seng Index surged 426.13 points, or 2.97 percent, last week to close at an all-time high of 14,757.81 on Friday.
"It would not be surprising to see a consolidation ahead of a push through 15,000," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
But brokers said liquidity flowing in from the mainland and regional funds would allow Hong Kong share prices to hold firm.
"I think we will remain at high levels. There is hot money coming in and in anticipation of the handover, we will have a surge," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on midnight of June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule.

Analysts said one of the key confidence indicators in the territory, its property market, was showing signs of picking up after a slowdown following government moves in late March to curb escalating prices. Property stocks represent about a third of the Hang Seng Index and any gains would give the market a boost.
"If there is more positive evidence in the property market, investors may try to pick up good value property stocks," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.

Analysts said the government's last land auction ahead of the change in sovereignty would be a focus this coming week. Two major residential sites -- a 571,848 square-foot (53,195 square metre) plot in beachside Stanley on Hong Kong Island and a 79,675 sq ft waterfront site in Kowloon's Hunghom -- will be sold on Tuesday.
"People are waiting to see what prices property developers are willing to bid at the auction," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.

He said investors may be a little cautious ahead of the auction. "Next week, I think you will see some consolidation. Several major U.S. economic figures will be released and investors will look to those as an indication of how interest rates will go at the next FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting in July," Lui added.
U.S. personal income and consumption data for April is due on Monday, leading indicators on Tuesday and the May employment report on Friday.

Benefun International Holdings Ltd is due to make its market debut on Tuesday. The casual wear retailer offered 100 million shares at HK$1.15 per share and the initial public offering was 105 times oversubscribed.
